title: Briefing: Albania, the Cockroach Janta Party, and Italy's protests
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Tuesday, October twentieth. It's read by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.

Student protests against Prime Minister Edi Rama's government have turned violent in Tirana. Albania's health ministry says two hundred seventy-two people have been injured since October fourteenth, including one hundred sixty-nine police officers; that's confirmed by independent reports. What's next: arrest figures for the weekend's violence, and whether students and the government begin talks.

The Cockroach Janta Party movement began in India as a satirical response to a judge's remark about unemployed youth, and now wants the country's chief election commissioner to resign over a disputed voter-roll revision. A Delhi court has extended the custody of two movement spokespeople by two more days without explaining why; that's confirmed by independent reports. What's next: whether everyone detained this month has been released, and the legal basis for that extension.

Students and cost-of-living protesters have been marching against Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government, and clashed with police in Milan for a second straight night as groups described by police as mostly minors looted stores; that's confirmed by independent reports. The Italian news agency and Fanpage give different police-injury tallies for the two nights of clashes, from fourteen to one hundred four officers hurt. What's next: whether the government adopts its planned security decree, and a single reconciled count of arrests and injuries.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
